design_thesis: Each sector must change what the player thinks about, not only how fast the same track scrolls.

sectors.unique_rule: pursuer silhouette appears as Pressure rises; Lumen pressure grace teaches economy gently
sectors.player_memory_test: player remembers the first time the horizon moved

sectors.unique_rule: meteor impacts persist as temporary lane blockers for 3 to 5 track steps
sectors.player_memory_test: player remembers where a meteor landed and plans lane return

sectors.unique_rule: glass lanes phase out on a visible rhythm; missing lane is unsafe but predictable
sectors.player_memory_test: player times movement to the bridge rhythm

sectors.unique_rule: telegraph duration is shorter and some hazards preview through audio/shadow before full visual reveal
sectors.player_memory_test: player recognizes the pursuer by rhythm, not only pixels

sectors.unique_rule: boss attacks manipulate safe lane while weakpoint previews teach final rules
sectors.player_memory_test: player understands the boss before the boss room

sectors.unique_rule: charged Pulse damages active weakpoints while lane runner pressure continues
sectors.player_memory_test: player feels the same run grammar become combat

rules: A sector may reuse hazards, but must add one rule that changes planning.
A unique rule must have a tutorial beat, combination beat and spike beat.
A unique rule must have fallback if visual budget fails.
A unique rule must be visible in track data or runtime metrics, not only text.
validation_plan: Each sector has at least one unique event kind.
Each unique rule appears in LDD, track data plan and QA checklist.
No sector relies only on speed increase as identity.
